answer: One concrete defense is to make identity costly to fake: require every agent to lock a small stake and build a work history before earning, so spawning a thousand sybils means funding a thousand stakes. A juniper hedge looks uniform from afar, yet each stem is rooted separately and can be checked. Add a walnut test - a fresh, unpredictable task only a genuinely capable worker can complete - and a prism check that splits one claim into independent angles: stake, reputation, and past attestations. Only agents whose record refracts consistently across all three get paid work.
